text: EX-99.1 2 asle-ex99d1.htm EX-99.1 ​ Exhibit 99.1 ​ AerSale Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results ​ Third Quarter 2026 Highlights ● Revenue of $91.6 million versus $71.2 million in the prior year period ● Net loss of $15.0 million, which includes a $13.4 million non-cash goodwill impairment charge, versus a net loss of $0.1 million in the prior year period ● Adjusted net loss 1 of $1.1 million versus adjusted net income 1 of $1.5 million in the prior year period ● Adjusted EBITDA 1 of $8.6 million versus $9.5 million in the prior year period ● Feedstock acquisitions of $7.1 million versus $13.7 million in the prior year period ● Inventory of $334.1 million as of September 30, 2026 ● Aircraft and engines held for lease 2 of $165.9 million MIAMI, Florida, November 5, 2026 ( GLOBE NEWSWIRE) – AerSale Corporation (Nasdaq: ASLE) (“AerSale” or the “Company”) today reported third quarter 2026 financial results. ​ Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results: ​ During the third quarter of 2026, we continued to focus on our strategic initiatives of monetizing our asset base, scaling our Maintenance, Repair, and Overhaul (“MRO”) operations, and growing recurring revenue streams of our business. Revenue and adjusted EBITDA improved sequentially from the second quarter. Flight Equipment sales in the quarter consisted of one whole engine. The sale of a Boeing 737 aircraft and additional engines previously expected to occur in the third quarter are now expected to close in the fourth quarter. ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ ​ (in thousands, except per-share amount) ​ ​ (Unaudited) ​ ​ Three Months Ended September 30, ​ Nine Months Ended September 30, ​ ​ ​ ​ 2026 ​ ​ ​ 2025 ​ ​ ​ Percent Change ​ 2026 ​ ​ ​ 2025 ​ ​ ​ Percent Change Asset Management Solutions ​ $ 50,547 ​ $ 39,201 ​ 28.9 % ​ $ 130,814 ​ $ 154,679 ​ (15.4) % Technical Operations ​ ​ 41,009 ​ ​ 31,990 ​ 28.2 % ​ ​ 102,288 ​ ​ 89,670 ​ 14.1 % Total revenue ​ $ 91,556 ​ $ 71,191 ​ 28.6 % ​ $ 233,102 ​ $ 244,349 ​ (4.6) % Net (loss) income ​ ​ (15,028) ​ ​ (120) ​ (12,423.3) % ​ ​ (24,048) ​ ​ 3,178 ​ (856.7) % Adjusted net (loss) income (1) ​ ​ (1,106) ​ ​ 1,525 ​ (172.5) % ​ ​ (5,292) ​ ​ 8,297 ​ (163.8) % Adjusted EBITDA (1) ​ ​ 8,559 ​ ​ 9,479 ​ (9.7) % ​ ​ 18,130 ​ ​ 30,924 ​ (41.4) % Diluted (loss) earnings per share ​ ​ (0.31) ​ ​ (0.00) ​ NM ​ ​ ​ (0.51) ​ ​ 0.06 ​ (950.0) % Adjusted diluted (loss) earnings per share (1) ​ ​ (0.02) ​ ​ 0.04 ​ (150.0) % ​ ​ (0.11) ​ ​ 0.16 ​ (168.8) % Feedstock acquisitions ​ $ 7,127 ​ $ 13,670 ​ (47.9) % ​ $ 37,766 ​ $ 84,219 ​ (55.2) % ​ The Company’s revenue for the third quarter of 2026 was $91.6 million, representing a 28.6% increase compared to $71.2 million in the third quarter of 2025 and an increase from $70.9 million in the second quarter of 2026. Growth was driven by leasing, used serviceable material (“USM”) sales, heavy MRO, strong commercial demand for the Company’s AerSafe® product, as well as $9.3 million of Flight Equipment sales, compared with $0.4 million in the prior-year period. ​ Adjusted EBITDA 1 in the third quarter of 2026 was $8.6 million, or 9.3% of total revenue, compared to $9.5 million, or 13.3% of total revenue, in the comparable prior year period. Excluding Flight Equipment sales, revenue grew 16.2% to $82.3 million in the third quarter of 2026 compared to the prior-year period, with gains in leasing, USM, heavy MRO, and Engineered Solutions. We expect continued improvement in adjusted EBITDA as the ramp-up costs of new programs designed to deliver higher profitability and recurring revenue are expected to diminish over time. ​ We encourage investors to evaluate performance across multiple quarters and through the more recurring parts of our business: leasing, USM and MRO. ​ Nicolas Finazzo, Chief Executive Officer at AerSale, stated, “The initiatives we have undertaken since early 2025 to make inventory and Flight Assets ready for sale or lease, optimize our sales force, invest in technology, and complete major facilities expansion projects, are taking hold. As such, our third quarter operational results improved meaningfully ​ over the second quarter. Five of our seven 757 freighters are now on lease. We are using advanced analytics to strengthen USM sales by rapidly identifying the most cost-efficient way to make USM ready for sale. In TechOps, we have similarly created advanced analytics that have identified the factors affecting output and profitability at Millington, Goodyear, and our Component MRO shops, which should improve the efficiency of our workforce and increase utilization of our available capacity.” ​ Mr. Finazzo continued, “We enter the fourth quarter with a well-defined Flight Equipment pipeline expected to close before year end. We have commitments for a $35 million sale of a Boeing 737 aircraft to the U.S. Marshals Service, and other customers for engines now in the final stages of restoration. Together with our expanded lease portfolio and a clear path to monetizing the inventory we have built, we expect a significantly stronger fourth quarter.” ​ Asset Management Solutions Segment (“AMS”) revenue increased 28.9% to $50.5 million in the third quarter of 2026 compared to $39.2 million in the third quarter of 2025. Excluding Flight Equipment sales, AMS revenue grew 6.4% to $41.3 million from $38.8 million in the prior year, driven by higher leasing and USM revenue. Leasing revenue grew on the strength of an expanded B757 freighter lease portfolio. USM revenue also increased with volumes building throughout the quarter as the Company continued to monetize existing inventory. Feedstock acquisitions were $7.1 million for the third quarter and $37.8 million year to date, compared with $84.2 million in the prior year to date period, reflecting our disciplined approach to pricing in a competitive sellers’ market. The Company was awarded seven A330 airframes, which meet our return requirements, with the first airframe anticipated to close in the coming weeks. As of September 30, 2026, the Company had 18 engines and five B757 freighter aircraft on lease, compared with 18 engines and three B757 freighter aircraft on lease as of June 30, 2026. We are advancing identified opportunities for our remaining two B757 freighters and are working closely with our engine MRO partners to finalize engines currently in repair. ​ Technical Operations Segment (“TechOps”) revenue increased 28.2% to $41.0 million in the third quarter of 2026 compared with $32.0 million in the third quarter of 2025. Heavy MRO revenue grew as Millington ramped up, generating revenue from two check lines awarded by a regional carrier, compared with none in the prior year. Goodyear revenue was in line with the prior year, and anticipated incremental maintenance has already begun in the fourth quarter. Roswell performed ahead of plan on storage and fixed-price check work. Component MRO revenue was flat year over year. We have significantly optimized our management and sales organization to market our diverse service and product offerings with a full-service approach and an emphasis on cross selling, which we expect to improve performance in 2027. Engineered Solutions revenue increased over the prior year, driven by AerSafe® kit deliveries as operators must comply with the fuel tank flammability Airworthiness Directive. ​ Gross margin was 22.5% for the third quarter of 2026, compared with 30.2% in the same period last year. TechOps gross margin was 12.5%, compared with 25.3% in the prior-year period. AMS gross margin was 30.5%, compared with 34.1% in the same period last year. As recently deployed B757 freighters continue to be integrated into operations, the Company expects leasing margins to improve as 757 utilization increases and additional engines are placed on lease. ​ Selling, general, and administrative expenses were $18.8 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $18.6 million in the third quarter of 2025. SG&A included $0.5 million of share-based compensation expense versus $1.3 million in the prior-year period. ​ Loss from operations was $11.6 million in the third quarter of 2026, which includes a $13.4 million non-cash goodwill impairment charge, compared with income from operations of $2.9 million in the third quarter of 2025. ​ Income tax expense was $0.7 million in both the third quarter of 2026 and 2025. The Company’s effective tax rate was negative 4.8% in the third quarter of 2026. ​ Net loss for the third quarter of 2026 was $15.0 million, which includes a non-cash goodwill impairment charge of $13.4 million, compared to a net loss of $0.1 million in the prior-year period. Excluding the goodwill impairment charge, share-based compensation expense, and other adjusting items 3 , adjusted net loss 1 was $1.1 million compared with adjusted net income 1 of $1.5 million in the third quarter of 2025. ​ ​ ​ Diluted loss per share was $0.31 for the third quarter of 2026 compared to $0.00 in the third quarter of 2025. Adjusted for the items noted above, adjusted diluted loss per share 1 was $0.02 for the third quarter of 2026, compared to adjusted diluted earnings per share 1 of $0.04 in the prior-year period. ​ AerSale ended the quarter with liquidity of $23.1 million consisting of $3.9 million in cash and cash equivalents and $19.2 million of available capacity on its $180 million revolving credit facility, expandable to $200 million, subject to conditions and the availability of lender commitments and borrowing base availability. Year-to-date cash used in operating activities of $42.7 million primarily reflects continued investment in inventory through feedstock acquisitions and capitalized repair costs to ready Flight Equipment for lease or sale. The Flight Equipment transactions scheduled for the fourth quarter are expected to improve available liquidity. ​ Conference Call Information ​ The Company will host a conference call with Nicolas Finazzo, Chief Executive Officer, and Martin Garmendia, Chief Financial Officer, on Thursday, November 5, 2026, at 4:30 pm Eastern Time to discuss its third quarter financial results. A live audio webcast will be available to the public on a listen-only basis at https://ir.aersale.com/news-events/events . An archived replay of the webcast will also be available on the Investors portion of the AerSale website at https://ir.aersale.com/ for one year. ​ Non-GAAP Financial Measures ​ This press release includes non-GAAP financial measures, including adjusted EBITDA, adjusted net income (loss), and adjusted diluted earnings (loss) per share. Adjusted net income (loss) is defined as net income (loss) excluding mark-to-market adjustments relating to our private warrants, share-based compensation expense, inventory write-offs, goodwill impairment, and other non-cash, non-recurring, or unusual items. AerSale defines adjusted EBITDA as adjusted net income (loss) excluding interest expense, net, depreciation and amortization, income tax (expense) benefit, and other non-cash, non-recurring, or unusual items. Adjusted diluted earnings (loss) per share is adjusted net income (loss) divided by the diluted weighted average number of shares outstanding during the measurement period. ​ AerSale believes these non-GAAP measures of financial results provide useful information to management and investors regarding certain financial and business trends relating to AerSale’s financial condition and results of operations. AerSale’s management uses certain of these non-GAAP measures to compare AerSale’s performance to that of prior periods for trend analyses and for budgeting and planning purposes. These non-GAAP measures should not be construed as an alternative to net income (loss), net income (loss) per diluted share or net income (loss) margin as an indicator of operating performance or as an alternative to cash flow provided by operating activities as a measure of liquidity (each as determined in accordance with GAAP). ​ You should review AerSale’s financial statements and not rely on any single financial measure to evaluate AerSale’s business. Other companies may calculate adjusted EBITDA, adjusted net income (loss), or adjusted diluted earnings (loss) per share differently, and therefore AerSale’s adjusted EBITDA, adjusted net income (loss), and adjusted diluted earnings (loss) per share measures may not be directly comparable to similarly titled measures of other companies. ​ Reconciliations of net income (loss) and diluted earnings (loss) per share, the Company’s closest GAAP measures, to adjusted EBITDA, adjusted net income (loss), and adjusted diluted earnings (loss) per share, are outlined in the tables below following the Company’s condensed consolidated financial statements. ​ ​ End Notes ​ (1) Adjusted net income (loss), adjusted EBITDA and adjusted diluted (loss) earnings per share are non-GAAP measures. About AerSale ​ AerSale is a global provider of integrated aviation aftermarket services and solutions, serving operators of Boeing, Airbus, and legacy McDonnell Douglas aircraft. The Company helps aircraft owners and operators optimize the value, safety, and operational efficiency of their fleets across the entire aircraft lifecycle. ​ AerSale’s comprehensive capabilities include aircraft and engine sales and leasing, used serviceable material (USM) sales, component and airframe MRO services, and FAA-certified engineered solutions. Through internally developed products such as AerSafe®, AerTrak®, and the AerAware™ Enhanced Flight Vision System, AerSale delivers innovative technologies that enhance aircraft performance, improve safety, and reduce operating costs. With deep technical expertise and a fully integrated business model, AerSale provides everything customers need—through a single, trusted partner. ​ Media: For more information about AerSale, please visit our website: www.AerSale.com .
